**Lands in:** `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/undeclared-field-write-driver-split.integration.test.ts` (or a sibling) for the hook-body / action-body `ctx.api` write, and a `packages/cli` integration test for the flow `create_record` / `update_record` node half (the only package that already declares `service-automation` plus both drivers). Assertions per the ADR-0112 envelope rule — `code: 'INVALID_FIELD'` **and** `status: 400`, never a bare `toThrow()` — plus "nothing stored, no shadow column" on both driver families. #13858 has landed, so the three lint messages this pins are live prose today; the scratch harness that measured all six runs green is the template. p3: pins only; no behaviour changes.

Size/model suggestion: S–M, `sonnet`/`opus`.

Same-batch siblings #14932 (`packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts`) and #14849 (`packages/rest/src/*.test.ts`) are disjoint.

### ⭐ The measurement already exists — you are making it durable, ⛔ not re-discovering it

#13858's dev drove all six cases and got a single answer: `INVALID_FIELD` / **400**, `Unknown field 'stagee' on object 'deal'`, with nothing stored on either driver family and **no shadow column on the schemaless one**. Real QuickJS sandbox, real bodies through `hookBodyRunnerFactory` / `actionBodyRunnerFactory`, real `ObjectQL`, the real `AutomationEngine` with the real builtin CRUD node executors, real `driver-sql` (better-sqlite3) and real `driver-memory`.

⚠️ **That harness was a scratch and was deleted** — the dispatch fenced committed `packages/runtime/**` changes out of #13858 and told the seat to *report* a warranted pin rather than add one. This card is that report being cashed. ⛔ So do not treat "the behaviour is X" as inherited fact: re-drive it. If your run disagrees with the six results above, that is a finding and outranks this card.

### What must be covered, and why it is not already

The existing file pins two shapes on both driver families — an L2 **body-written** undeclared key, and a **caller-supplied** one. Neither covers the two shapes whose author-facing lint prose #13858 rewrote:

1. `ctx.api.object(x).update({...})` carrying an undeclared key, issued **from inside a hook body** *and* **from inside an action body** (`validate-hook-body-writes.ts`'s `ctx.api` branch, `validate-action-body-writes.ts`);
2. a flow `create_record` / `update_record` node's `fields` map (`validate-flow-node-writes.ts`).

⭐ **Why a pin and not a note:** three lint messages now assert "INVALID_FIELD / 400, identically on every driver/datasource, before any statement is built" — and one of them, `validate-flow-node-writes`, is `severity: 'error'`, i.e. it **gates**. The corroborating pin is about a *different call shape*, so if the door moves for the `ctx.api` or flow-node paths specifically, every gate stays green and three author-facing sentences quietly become wrong. That is the exact failure mode #13858 was filed to fix, one layer down.

### Non-negotiable on the assertions

⛔ **ADR-0112 envelope rule: assert `code` AND `status`, never a bare `toThrow()`.** A `toThrow()` passes on the wrong error, which on this card would pin the opposite of what it claims.

### Suggested route (optional; measurement beats it)

The card suggests two `it.each(FAMILIES)` blocks in the existing file's idiom, or a sibling file. Either is fine. ⚠️ The flow half needs `service-automation` **plus both drivers in one package** — `packages/cli` is the only one declaring all three, which is why that half lands there rather than beside the hook/action half. Confirm that dependency claim before committing to the location.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #15370, **including its one deviation, which I am ruling correct.** Reviewed against GitHub, ⛔ not against the report.

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024), R69, session `session_01D47qPfEWVPmhguWgBZCi5N`. Reviewer of record.

### Checklist

| item | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| draft · base `main` · `Fixes #14241` | ✅ |
| ⛔ pins only — no source, no lint-rule edit | ✅ **2 files, +510 / −2**, both test files |
| ADR-0112: `code` **and** `status`, ⛔ never a bare `toThrow()` | ✅ on every refusal case |
| both `ctx.api` shapes (hook body **and** action body) | ✅ two `it.each(FAMILIES)` blocks in the ruled file's own idiom |
| flow `create_record` **and** `update_record` | ✅ new `packages/cli` file, real `AutomationEngine`, real builtin CRUD executors, real `ObjectQL`, real `driver-sql` |
| "nothing stored, no shadow column" | ✅ target row untouched, no shadow column, and the write that triggered the body refused with it |
| `skip-changeset` | ✅ test-only |

### 🔨 The deviation — one driver family on the flow half. **Ruled: correct, and I would have ruled the same way.**

My dispatch asked for both families. The dev ran one and said why: a `driver-memory` import in `packages/cli` would be an **unledgered arrival** under `scripts/driver-memory-census.ledger.json`, gated by `check:driver-memory-census` (#6664, from #5704 / #5499). Admitting a new test consumer of that frozen driver is a **maintainer ruling**, and would additionally force rewriting the census sentence in two existing ruled files.

⭐ **Stopping there was right.** That gate encodes a governed decision about a frozen package; editing the ledger to satisfy my dispatch would have been a test author quietly taking a maintainer's call — the exact shape this repo's shrink-only ledgers exist to prevent. ⛔ I am not overriding my own fence retroactively: the fence was "pins only", and the ledger is not a pin.

**And what replaced the second arm is stronger than a second sample, not a concession.** The lint prose says the refusal is "identical on every datasource" — and it is identical *because no driver is reached at all*. So the flow file **counts every write verb the real driver is asked to perform and asserts zero** on each refusal case. A family split cannot arise below a door nothing gets past; two samples would have demonstrated the same thing twice and still not proven it. Meanwhile the schemaless persistence half for this exact payload shape stays pinned on **both** families by the ruled runtime file's caller-payload block — which is sound, because a flow node's `fields` map *is* a caller payload.

The same constraint explains why the `ctx.api` half extends the ruled file rather than landing in a sibling: a sibling needs its own `driver-memory` import, i.e. the same unledgered arrival. `check:driver-memory-census` is green.

⇒ Both files document this in place, which is the right home for it — better than a card, because the next author who wonders "why only one family here?" is reading the file, not the backlog.

### ⭐ A card claim was corrected, and correctly

The card said the flow pin should assert "the node's error names the refusal". The dev found the step's error is an **envelope** — `{ code: 'NODE_FAILURE', message: "create_record(deal) failed: Unknown field 'stagee' on object 'deal'" }` — so the door's `INVALID_FIELD` **does not reach a run's step**; only its message survives the fold.

⭐ It then checked whether that is a defect and established it is **deliberate**: `crud-nodes.ts` narrows code re-surfacing to `DUPLICATE_RECORD`, and `engine.ts` carries `result.code` to the branchable `{$error.code}` variable instead. ⇒ It pinned **the observed truth** — the whole envelope, so a reader can see the code does not survive — and asserted the door's own `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 at the seam where code and status are still observable. That is the difference between pinning what the card assumed and pinning what the system does.

The other card claim I asked it to confirm also holds: `packages/cli` **is** the only package declaring `service-automation` and both drivers, checked across the eleven packages declaring `service-automation` at all.

### ⭐ A moved ratchet was FIXED, not baselined

`check:query-options-erasure` went red — test surface 236 → 241 — from five new `as any` options bags. The dev rewrote them through typed `EngineQueryOptions` helpers; the ratchet reports "holds … 236 site(s) — at the ceiling", **no baseline edit**. That is the shrink-only rule working as intended: the fix is the errors, not the ceiling.

### Measurement re-driven, not inherited

All six shapes re-driven and all six agree with #13858's deleted scratch harness: `INVALID_FIELD` / 400, `Unknown field 'stagee' on object 'deal'`, nothing stored, no shadow column. ⇒ The report is cashed rather than trusted, which is what the dispatch asked for.

**Ablation** — mutation is declaring `stagee` on the DEAL fixture, i.e. *the single input the door's verdict reads*, which faithfully stands in for "the door stopped refusing undeclared keys on this path". runtime **22 passed → 16 failed / 6 passed**; cli **7 passed → 5 failed / 2 passed**. Every refusal case red on both families and all five flow cases; only the controls stayed green — correct, since they do not depend on `stagee` being undeclared. Mutation proved on disk by injected-marker grep **plus** `hash-object` against the HEAD blobs; restore proved by empty `git diff HEAD`, both hashes back, marker count 0.

⭐ And the no-rebuild reasoning is stated rather than assumed: the mutated text is each test file's **own fixture** (vitest compiles it from source), while the subject under test resolves through `dist`, built beforehand and untouched — so no dist preflight applies. Knowing *when* a dist preflight is and is not owed is the part most reports get wrong in the other direction.

### Landing

⏳ Flip and enqueue held pending CI convergence. Path fork clean — two test files under `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/` and `packages/cli/src/`; no governed surface. Goes to the queue on a full green — **every** check, ⛔ not the required subset.
